whyChoose.title: Why Timing and Facts Matter in California

items.title: The Clock Is Ticking
items.desc: California generally gives you two years from the date of injury to file a personal injury claim, though claims against a government agency may require notice in as little as six months. Waiting too long can mean losing your right to recover.

items.title: Shared Fault Won't Shut You Out
items.desc: California follows pure comparative fault, so even if you were partly responsible for the crash, you may still recover compensation reduced by your share of fault. This applies whether the accident happened on Sperry Avenue or anywhere else in town.

items.title: No Ceiling on Certain Damages
items.desc: In ordinary injury cases, California places no cap on non-economic damages like pain and suffering. That means compensation isn't artificially limited to medical bills and lost wages alone.

items.title: You Pay Nothing Upfront
items.desc: Our team works on contingency, so there's no fee unless we win or settle your case. This lets injured people pursue a claim without worrying about hourly legal fees.

items.question: How long do I have to file a personal injury claim in Patterson?
items.answer: California law generally allows two years from the date of the injury to file a claim. If a government entity is involved, such as a city vehicle or a hazard on public property, the deadline to file a claim notice can be as short as six months. It's best not to wait, since evidence and witness memories fade quickly.

items.question: What if I was partly at fault for the accident?
items.answer: California uses pure comparative fault, which means you can still recover compensation even if you share some responsibility for the crash. Your total recovery would simply be reduced by your percentage of fault. This applies to car accidents, falls, and most other injury claims.

items.question: Where do crashes tend to happen in Patterson?
items.answer: Public collision records show that corridors like Sperry Avenue, 2nd Street, Route 33, and Las Palmas Avenue have some of the higher reported collision counts in the city. Reported crashes also tend to cluster on Friday afternoons between 3 and 5 p.m. These are simply neutral, publicly reported patterns, not a judgment about any particular road.

items.question: Does it cost anything to contact us?

items.question: How much will an attorney charge if I have a case?
items.answer: Our team works on a contingency basis, meaning we only get paid if we recover compensation for you through a settlement or verdict. There are no upfront fees to have your case reviewed.
